requirements.title: Deallocating an unallocated allocatable variable is a DEALLOCATE error condition
requirements.definition: Executing a DEALLOCATE statement for an allocatable variable that is unallocated causes an error condition in that DEALLOCATE statement. The STAT value and post-error status are owned by 9.7.4; this requirement does not invent a static diagnostic duty.

requirements.title: Deallocating an allocatable TARGET makes associated pointer statuses undefined
requirements.definition: When an allocatable variable with the TARGET attribute is deallocated, the pointer association status of every pointer associated with it becomes undefined. Because undefined pointer association status is not a portable executable oracle, future tests must avoid querying or dereferencing those pointers after the deallocation.

requirements.title: Unsaved allocatable procedure locals are deallocated on RETURN or END except function results
requirements.definition: When procedure execution terminates by RETURN or END, an unsaved allocatable local variable retains its allocation and definition status if it is a function result or a subobject of a function result. Otherwise, an unsaved allocatable local variable that is allocated is deallocated.

requirements.title: INTENT(OUT) invocation deallocates corresponding allocated allocatable actuals and subobjects

requirements.title: Coarray deallocation synchronizes active images and succeeds only on all active images
requirements.definition: Executing a statement that deallocates a coarray or an object with a coarray potential subobject component includes implicit synchronization of all active images in the current team. A stopped or failed image in the current team causes an error condition. If no other error occurs, active images are delayed after the statement until all other active images in the current team have executed the same statement the same number of times in that team; segments before the statement on an active image precede segments after the statement on another active image; and a coarray shall not become deallocated on an image unless it is successfully deallocated on all active images in the team.
